Ollama's documentation is inconsistent about the default context length, and the sources I found disagree on the number.

- **Conflicting defaults:** One guide says Ollama's FAQ page still states that the default context window is 4096 tokens, overridable with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH. Another notes that the Modelfile reference says the num_ctx default is 2048, while the context length page says the default depends on available VRAM. The binary's help text reads default: 4k/32k/256k based on VRAM. A harn-vm source file sets its own fallback of 32,768.
- **Setting it server-wide:** OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH sets the default for every request that does not carry its own num_ctx. The docs show an example of OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=64000 ollama serve.
- **Per-request or per-model:** Setting num_ctx on a request takes precedence over the server default. Inside an interactive session, you can use /set parameter num_ctx 8192.
- **Truncation is silent:** One source says that when input exceeds the window, Ollama does not abort execution or display an error message in the terminal. A related symptom is Ollama will use its default (4096) unless the underlying model in Ollama is configured for a higher context window.
- **Memory cost:** Setting a larger context length will increase the amount of memory required to run a model. To check what is actually in use, the docs suggest verifying the split under PROCESSOR using ollama ps.

Most of these sources are third-party guides, so for the current default on a given version, check the Ollama source or the release notes directly.

input.ask: Should I try a local model in the real app through the developer address override?

content.text:
My recommendation is to add one "local model" provider, not one per runtime. All the popular local runtimes now accept the two request formats the app already sends, so a single provider with an address the person can change covers them all. The real risk isn't the API. It's whether a small model on someone's laptop can handle the app's tools. This is a proposal: nothing is built or tested.

## What the app does today

The app sends one of two request formats: the OpenAI Responses format (used for OpenAI, OpenRouter and the JusPrin gateway) or the Anthropic Messages format. Each provider is a row in the table in [ProviderProfile.hpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProviderProfile.hpp). Every row has a fixed address and needs an API key. The app also refuses to start a chat unless the person has agreed to cloud access.

## The popular runtimes

- **Ollama**: the most common one. It has served the Responses format since v0.13.3, without saved server-side conversations, which the app doesn't use. It has served the Messages format since v0.14.0 (January 2026). It runs at `localhost:11434` and needs no key.
- **LM Studio**: a desktop app that also runs Apple's MLX engine. Responses format since 0.3.29, Messages format since 0.4.1. It runs at `localhost:1234`, and a key is optional.
- **llama.cpp (`llama-server`)**: the engine under most of the others. It has served the Messages format since January 2026. A July 2026 change added the Responses format, but I couldn't confirm which release it shipped in.
- **Others**: Jan, LocalAI, Docker Model Runner and vLLM. vLLM is for GPU servers, not desktops. They all advertise OpenAI-style APIs, so the same provider row should reach them.

## The proposal

1. **One provider called "Local model".** It uses the Responses format, needs no key, and its address starts at Ollama's and can be changed to LM Studio's or any other. I'd expect the model list to work as it is, because these runtimes answer `/v1/models` in OpenAI's format. I haven't checked that.
2. **No cloud-consent gate** for this provider, since nothing leaves the machine.
3. **No web-search tool** in its requests. Every row sends the provider's own web search, and local runtimes have none.
4. **A test before anything else.** Each request carries about 41,000 characters of tool definitions for 30–32 tools, which I measured in your saved requests. That's roughly 11,000 tokens before any history, and history can add up to 64 KiB. On a machine with little graphics memory, Ollama defaults to a 4,096-token context and cuts the rest off silently. The model would then act strangely with no error at all. So the first step is to run the existing evals against a couple of local models, at a context of 32k or more, and see whether they cope.

The test can start today without new code. The developer override `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT` can point the OpenAI row at `http://localhost:11434/v1/responses` with a dummy key.

## Decision needed

What should the app tell someone whose local model can't run it? This happens when the model has no tool support, or when the runtime's context is too small for the tools. Unlike an outage, the person can fix it, by picking another model or raising the context. Under the error-handling rules that makes it an expected error, and expected errors need your yes on the wording. The first option is one sentence covering both cases, such as "This model can't run the app's tools; pick a model with tool support and a context of at least 32k." It's cheap and follows the rule that two causes with the same fix share one sentence. The second option is no special handling: the failures get reported as generic errors. That costs nothing now, but people with a too-small context would see a confused AI and no explanation. I'd pick the one sentence, once the test shows how these failures actually look. Do you want that sentence, or no special handling?

Should I try a local model in the real app through the override now, or leave it for later?

Sources: [Ollama OpenAI compatibility](https://docs.ollama.com/api/openai-compatibility), [Ollama Anthropic compatibility](https://docs.ollama.com/api/anthropic-compatibility), [Ollama context length](https://docs.ollama.com/context-length), [silent truncation write-up](https://particula.tech/blog/ollama-num-ctx-silent-prompt-truncation), [LM Studio 0.3.29](https://lmstudio.ai/changelog/lmstudio-v0.3.29), [LM Studio Anthropic compatibility](https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/anthropic-compat), [llama.cpp Messages API](https://huggingface.co/blog/ggml-org/anthropic-messages-api-in-llamacpp), [llama.cpp Responses change](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26045), [runtime comparison](https://machinelearningmastery.com/ollama-vs-lm-studio-vs-llama-cpp-which-local-ai-runtime-should-you-use-in-2026/)

description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."

---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

description: "Traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control: in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args and @import failures, the model picker needs page JS, a debugger attach once hung a slice."
metadata:

  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439

---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **`@import AppKit` can fail silently in lldb `expr`** ("no known method '-windows'"). Then cast everything to `id` and get classes with `((Class(*)(const char*))objc_getClass)("NSApplication")`; a working runner that runs a JS file in the chat panel (title "JusPrin Agent") was `runjs.sh` in the 2026-11-12 scratchpad.
- **The composer's model picker is a drop-down the background `app_click` refuses.** Click it from page JS via the runner above. OpenRouter's list labels models "Anthropic: Claude …", so a regex on "Claude Fable" picks OpenRouter's copy; the Anthropic-key one starts with "Claude".
- **A slice right after lldb attaches hung once (2026-11-12).** The worker sat in upstream `name_tbb_thread_pool_threads_set_locale()`, a barrier every TBB thread must reach, and the main thread waited in `BackgroundSlicingProcess::start()` forever. After a relaunch with no debugger the same slice ran at once. Suspected trigger: pausing the app while its thread pool was starting. Don't report such a hang as an app bug without a run that had no debugger attached.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

Builds on [[live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page]]; used 2026-11-02 when screen control of the app was denied.

- Page text input: native value setter plus an `input` event. A modal Preferences window's page polls as `agent-preferences`.
- A test preset needs a `version` field or import rejects it.
- A compose recreate drops env set by a wrapper; check `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` before any chat so only the fake upstream is reachable.

Still needs the screen: pointer hover, native file dialogs, Orca's wizard.

content.text:
I don't know yet if a good Mac can run a local model that works with the app, and nobody can without the test. A recent Mac with 16 GB of memory can hold a small model and the context it needs. My doubts are speed and how well a small model picks among the app's tools, and both are hypotheses.

**What fits.** Each request is about 11,000 tokens of tool definitions plus the system prompt and the chat history, so the model needs a context window of 32k tokens or more. Two models that fit:
- **qwen3.5:9b** is a 6.6 GB download. With that context it should fit on a 16 GB Mac. Its Ollama page lists tool use and pictures.
- **gpt-oss:20b** is a 13.8 GB download and needs 24–32 GB of memory. It can't read pictures, and the app sends a picture of the plate when a file is opened. So it can't stand in for the full experience.

**Speed: probably the problem.** A Mac has to read the whole request before it writes a word. Published numbers for 7–8B models on Apple chips are roughly 300–900 tokens per second for that reading, with the top M4 Max chips at the high end. If that holds, a base M2 or M3 MacBook would pause 20–60 seconds before the first request of a turn. A turn that calls several tools sends several requests, but each repeat should be faster, because Ollama keeps the part of the request it has already read. That's a guess from benchmarks, not a measurement.

**Quality: unknown, and the bigger risk.** Hosted models already miss steps in the app's evals. For example, gpt-5.4-mini skipped looking at the model in 3 of 3 test chats. A 9B model choosing among 30 tools could do worse.

**How I'd find out.** This Mac is an M2 Pro with 32 GB, close to a "pretty good Mac". I'd run qwen3.5:9b through the app's developer address override for a few real chats: open a file, ask it to prepare the print, change a setting. I'd measure the time before the first word of each turn and note whether it picks the right tools. Two caveats. Other sessions are keeping this machine busy (load 7–9 on 12 cores), so the times will read slow. The disk also has only 33 GB free.

**What has to be downloaded first.** The installed Ollama is version 0.3.13 from October 2024, which predates the request format the app sends. The test needs:
- The Ollama 0.40.17 upgrade, 231 MB, from Ollama's GitHub releases page. It replaces the old app in /Applications.
- The qwen3.5:9b model, 6.6 GB, from Ollama's model library. That leaves about 26 GB of disk.

Can I download both and run the test, or should I leave it for now?

"""Replay a saved JusPrin request body against a local Responses endpoint.

Usage: python3 replay.py <saved-request.json> [model] [endpoint]
Prints time to first output, total time, token usage, tool calls and text.
"""
import json
import sys
import time
import urllib.request

path = sys.argv[1]
model = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "qwen3.5:9b"
endpoint = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "http://localhost:11434/v1/responses"

body = json.load(open(path))["body"]
body["model"] = model
dropped = [t.get("type") for t in body.get("tools", []) if t.get("type") != "function"]
body["tools"] = [t for t in body.get("tools", []) if t.get("type") == "function"]


def strip_images(value):
    # The saved log replaced picture bytes with a note; such a part cannot be sent.
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [strip_images(v) for v in value
                if not (isinstance(v, dict) and v.get("type") in ("input_image", "input_file"))]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: strip_images(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    return value


before = json.dumps(body["input"])
body["input"] = strip_images(body["input"])
images_removed = before != json.dumps(body["input"])
# Reasoning items from another provider cannot be replayed.
body["input"] = [i for i in body["input"] if i.get("type") != "reasoning"]

req = urllib.request.Request(endpoint, data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                             headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": "Bearer local"})
start = time.time()
first = None
text = []
calls = []
usage = None
event_types = {}
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=900) as resp:
    for raw in resp:
        line = raw.decode().strip()
        if not line.startswith("data:"):
            continue
        data = line[5:].strip()
        if data == "[DONE]":
            break
        ev = json.loads(data)
        t = ev.get("type", "")
        event_types[t] = event_types.get(t, 0) + 1
        if first is None and t in ("response.output_text.delta", "response.reasoning_text.delta",
                                   "response.function_call_arguments.delta", "response.output_item.added"):
            first = time.time() - start
        if t == "response.output_text.delta":
            text.append(ev.get("delta", ""))
        if t == "response.output_item.done" and ev.get("item", {}).get("type") == "function_call":
            it = ev["item"]
            calls.append((it.get("name"), it.get("arguments")))
        if t in ("response.completed", "response.failed", "response.incomplete"):
            usage = ev.get("response", {}).get("usage")
            if t != "response.completed":
                print("END EVENT", t, json.dumps(ev.get("response", {}).get("error") or ev)[:500])
total = time.time() - start
print(f"file={path.split('/')[-1]} model={model} dropped_tools={dropped} images_removed={images_removed}")
print(f"first_output_s={first and round(first, 1)} total_s={round(total, 1)} usage={usage}")
for name, args in calls:
    print("CALL", name, (args or "")[:300])
print("TEXT", "".join(text)[:1500])

content.text:
The local model works with today's app and no code changes, but it isn't good enough to offer people yet. I ran the real app against qwen3.5:9b through Ollama on this M2 Pro with 32 GB. It called the right tools with sensible arguments, but it's slow and it gets facts wrong.

**What I ran.** I copied today's build and gave it a scratch data folder with every API key and printer access code removed. I pointed it at Ollama through the developer override (`JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT`) and opened your `rhino1-1.stl`. The app started its usual turn when the file opened, and then I asked it to "Slice it and tell me how long it will take and how much filament it uses." I also replayed four saved requests from an earlier chat straight to Ollama. Other sessions' builds were keeping the machine busy (load 19–24 on 12 cores), so these times are on the slow side.

**What worked.**
- Ollama accepted the app's requests as they are: the 30-odd tools, the plate picture, and the app's web-search tool, which it ignored without an error.
- The model list, the picture and tool calls all worked. On the slice request it called slice_start, then workspace_inspect, then slice_report, and reported the correct print time of about 7 hours.
- The tool definitions come to about 11,200 tokens, and the model fit in 7.6 GB of memory with a 32k context.

**Speed.**
- In the real chat, each request took 37–90 seconds, and the turn after opening the file took 4 minutes 24 seconds.
- In the replays, once the tool list was cached, the first word came after 3–7 seconds. In the real chat the picture and the changing messages seem to defeat that cache. That's a guess I haven't checked.
- One request ran past the app's 120-second limit per request (`request_timeout_seconds` in [AgentTransport.hpp:27](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentTransport.hpp:27)). The person saw "The AI request could not reach the OpenAI service." That limit would have to change for local models.

**Quality: the real blocker.**
- It called the rhino "a mechanical linkage… with threaded holes (M6–M10)", in both turns.
- The prompt says the first message after a file opens must change nothing unasked, but it repaired the mesh anyway.
- The slice report said 20.1 m of filament and no weight, because the default filament has no density. The model answered "around 230–250 grams" plus "7 meters of purge filament". 20.1 m of 1.75 mm PLA is about 60 g, so its figure was four times too high and the purge was made up.
- In the replays it once guessed setting names ("infill", "top_bottom_layers") instead of looking them up.

I didn't run a hosted model on the same file for comparison, because that costs API money. This is one conversation, so it's an observation, not a rate.

**State now.** Ollama is upgraded to 0.40.17 in /Applications. The old app is kept at `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth--claude-spares-spare-Nzsulp/27aeb673-3e7e-4b6a-bee5-c6666cf59545/scratchpad/ollama-dl/Ollama-0.3.13.app`. qwen3.5:9b stays on disk. Nothing I started is still running. I deleted the scratch data folder and kept the request logs and the app log in `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth--claude-spares-spare-Nzsulp/27aeb673-3e7e-4b6a-bee5-c6666cf59545/scratchpad/live/evidence/`.

**Decision needed.** Should local models be a product feature, or stay a developer setting for now? Making it a feature means a "Local model" provider in setup, a longer request limit for it, and the one-sentence error for models that can't run the tools. My guess is a few days of work, plus evals on a few models to set a minimum. The cost is support: on a 9B model people will get wrong facts and multi-minute turns, and they'll blame the app. Keeping it a developer setting costs nothing, because the override already works, and leaves room to revisit as small models improve. I'd pick the developer setting for now, and maybe a short note in the docs for enthusiasts.

# Plan: a model on this computer (Ollama, LM Studio and others)

Status: **proposal**. Nothing here is agreed except that Kenneth asked for a plan for a real feature (2026-11-24). Every on-screen sentence below is a draft.

## What the person gets

Someone who runs Ollama or LM Studio opens Preferences › Agent, chooses "A model on this computer", and sees the address the app will use (Ollama's `http://127.0.0.1:11434` filled in). They press Connect. The app lists the models that runtime has, they pick one, and the app checks it in one real request. If the model can use the app's tools and has room for them, the chat works like any other provider, with nothing leaving the computer. If not, they get one sentence saying what to change.

## What we know (measured 2026-11-24, M2 Pro, 32 GB, qwen3.5:9b on Ollama 0.40.17)

- The app's requests work on Ollama's `/v1/responses` unchanged: 30–33 tools, the plate picture, the app's web-search tool (ignored). The model list works from `/v1/models`.
- One request carries about 11,200 tokens before any history (the tool definitions are ~41,000 characters).
- Speed: in the real chat each request took 37–90 s and the turn after opening a file took 4 min 24 s. In replays without the picture, once the tool list was cached, the first word came in 3–7 s. My guess, not checked: the picture or the one-response developer message sits early in the input and stops Ollama reusing its cache.
- One request ran past the app's 120-second limit for a whole request (`request_timeout_seconds`, `Agent/AgentTransport.hpp:27`), and the person saw "The AI request could not reach the OpenAI service."
- Quality, one conversation: it called a rhino "a mechanical linkage with M6–M10 threaded holes", repaired the mesh when the prompt says change nothing unasked, and turned "20.1 m of filament" into "230–250 g" (about 60 g is right). Tool order on the slice request was right.
- Ollama's OpenAI-style endpoints cannot set the context size; only the server setting (`OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`) or a Modelfile can. Too small a context truncates silently. Ollama's `/api/show` reports a model's capabilities (`tools`, `vision`) and `/api/ps` the context it was loaded with. LM Studio's `/api/v1/models` reports `trained_for_tool_use` and the loaded context.
- A text-only model refuses any request with a picture: Ollama answers 400 "Multimodal data provided, but model does not support multimodal requests." The app sends the plate picture after every file open, so such a model fails on the first turn.

## Work, in order

1. **Measure which models are good enough, before any UI.** Run the existing live prompt suite (free on a local model) on qwen3.5:9b, gemma4:12b and one larger model, three runs each to start. This sets the bar and tells us whether a 16 GB Mac can meet it. If no model under ~16 GB passes, the feature's page says so, and it may not be worth building yet.
2. **A "local" provider row** in `ProviderProfile.hpp`: Responses format, no key, address from config (`jusprin_agent.local_endpoint`), no web-search tool (empty `web_search_type`, `ResponsesCodec` skips it), no cloud-consent gate (`resolve_agent_runtime`). Its name in errors comes from the runtime ("Ollama", "LM Studio", or "the model on this computer").
3. **Request time limit per row.** The local row gets no total limit (or a long one). Hosted rows keep 120 s. `Http` has only connect and total limits, so a stall detector, if wanted, is a separate change.
4. **Setup check** in Preferences › Agent, using the existing "verification is construction" probe (`AgentSetup.cpp`), with the full tool list so the check measures what a chat needs. Before the probe, ask the runtime what it can tell us: Ollama `/api/show` and `/api/ps`, LM Studio `/api/v1/models`. A runtime we don't recognize skips this check.
5. **Model picker**: the local provider's catalogue comes from `/v1/models`. Fix the composer label, which showed "gpt-5.4-mini" for a chat running qwen3.5:9b.
6. **Cache order** (only if step 1 shows speed is the blocker): check whether moving the picture after the stable part of the input makes the first word come in seconds rather than a minute. This touches every provider's request shape, so it gets its own test against hosted providers too.
7. **Boards first** (design-guidelines): the setup group, the address field, the model list, the check's states, and the one sentence for each expected error. Then code.
8. **Docs**: a `docs/HLSD/agent-providers.md` section on the local row, and a guide page "Use a model on your computer" with the context-size step for Ollama and LM Studio (it goes through the guide check before a release).
9. **Tests**: unit tests for the row (no key, no consent gate, no web-search tool, no time limit), for the setup check's reading of `/api/show`, `/api/ps` and `/api/v1/models` answers, and a live test tagged so it runs only where Ollama is present. Windows and Linux: same ports; use `127.0.0.1`, not `localhost`, so a Windows machine that resolves `localhost` to `::1` first doesn't miss Ollama.

Not needed: the Anthropic format (Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp serve it, but Responses already works and has fewer translation layers to go wrong), a bundled runtime, downloading models for the person.

## Decisions for Kenneth

1. Who it is for: any model that passes the check, or only models we have tested.
2. The expected errors and their sentences (each needs his yes): nothing answering at the address; the model can't use tools, or the context is too small.
3. Text-only models: refuse them at setup, or let them run with the plate picture left out of their requests.

# JusPrin design guidelines

**Status:** Canonical guidance for `jusprin-dev` on how a screen gets designed and checked, and on the words it shows. The visual system (tokens, type, color, components, logo) lives in [Design system](design-system.md); this document does not repeat it.

Design agents tend to write on-screen text that only they can read. The agent knows how the screen works, so a line like "The sixth digit signs you in." reads clearly to it and to any reviewer who knows the same. A person opening the app for the first time has to decode it, and often can't. The First-Launch Confusion Review (https://claude.ai/artifact/91wmdS3QU8UkzbPi1zog15, 2026-11-06) found 23 places on the first launch where a newcomer would misread or stall, and most of them were wording. The rules below exist to stop that at the source and to catch what still gets through.

## How a screen gets designed and checked

These steps apply to every change to text a person sees, not only to new screens: a new link on an existing board, a reworded line, or a one-sentence fix all get the cold-reader check on the board before building (step 5) and in the running app after (step 8).

1. **Start from the person.** Before drawing, write down in two or three sentences who reaches this screen, what they know at that moment, what they came to do, and what they must decide here. Every line on the screen serves one of those.
2. **Draw the whole screen, not a component alone.** A board for review is the full screen at the app's size, with the header, panes and neighbouring content the person really sees there, on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). Build it from the Design System artifact's coded components and the app's own markup, never by copying an older board. Repeated compositions are imported by name, as [Design handoff requirements](design-system.md#design-handoff-requirements) rule 9 says.
3. **Fill it with real strings.** Text that summarises data comes from the rule that will produce it in the app, run on real data. If only a model could write a line, say so on the board.
4. **Write every line by the wording rule below.**
5. **Run the cold-reader check on the boards** (below). Rewrite and check again until every line and button reads as intended.
6. **Show the board for review by what a person sees.** Name the screen as the person would ("the welcome screen, after typing an email"), give the canvas page it is on, and attach the picture. Board ids and builder labels mean nothing to a reviewer.
7. **Build it** following [Writing UI code](design-system.md#writing-ui-code).
8. **Check it in the running app.** Take screenshots of the built screen along one real path and run the cold-reader check again. The guards prove the code went through the tokens; only the screenshots show what the person reads.

## The cold-reader check

The writer of a screen cannot see that its text is cryptic, so the check is done by a reader who knows nothing about how the screen works.

- Start a fresh agent. Give it only the screenshots and one or two sentences a real user would know (for example: "You own a 3D printer and just installed JusPrin, a desktop app that prepares 3D models for printing."). Give it no code, spec, design notes, chat history or list of suspected problems, and rename files so their names don't hint at anything.
- Use screenshots from one coherent path, in the order a person meets them. Mixing signed-in and signed-out screens, or states set by hand, makes the reader report contradictions that no user would see.
- Ask it, for each screen, to quote every line and every button exactly, say in one plain sentence what the line means or what the button will do, and list where it would hesitate, misread, worry, or not know what to do next, including information the screen leaves out. Tell it to read literally, like a busy newcomer: a line it had to puzzle out counts as a problem even if it worked it out.
- Compare its answers with the intent written in step 1. Any line it reads differently from the intent gets rewritten, however small the gap. Its other hesitations are input to weigh, not orders.

What the check is known to catch: on 2026-11-06 a fresh agent given only the review's ten screenshots fully caught 14 of the 23 problems and partly caught 4 more. It caught every cryptic phrasing in the list. It missed problems that need knowledge from outside the screen (that Skip installs a 250 mm Klipper printer) and finer editorial calls (a redundant reassurance, one allowance under three names, "Connected" used for an account). It also raised real questions the review had not, such as what happens after the free month. It has not been compared with a real first-time user, so for the screens that matter most, such as first launch, a person remains the final test.

## Wording

Every line says what the person does or what happens to them, in a full sentence, in words a newcomer already has.

The five patterns below are what the review found most. Each pair is the text the app showed and the review's proposed rewrite; the rewrites are proposals, not yet in the app.

1. **Facts joined by a middle dot.** The dot drops how the facts relate, and the reader guesses.
   - Before: "Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits" (reads like a balance the person already had)
   - After: "You got 500 free credits for signing up.", with the email address on a smaller line under it
2. **Metaphors.** The reader has to work out what the image stands for.
   - Before: "New or existing account, same door."
   - After: a "Sign up free" button, with "Already have an account? Sign in" under it
   - Before: "Pick how the agent should think." (the options are ways to pay for or connect the agent)
   - After: "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice."
3. **Describing the mechanism instead of the action.** Say what the person does, not how the screen works inside.
   - Before: "The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device."
   - After: "Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone."
4. **Internal labels.** A name the team uses, shown nowhere else on the screen, explains nothing.
   - Before: "An Expert message is 5 credits."
   - After: the cost in things the person does, for example "500 credits is about 100 questions to the agent" (check the number against real costs)
5. **Hinting at a consequence instead of stating it.** If a choice changes what the person gets, say what it changes.
   - Before: "Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours."
   - After: "If you skip, files are sliced for a stand-in printer with a 250 mm bed, not for yours. Add your printer before you print anything. You can do that later on the home screen."

Space on a screen is tight, and short text looks finished. That is how these lines get written. Shorten only after the full sentence passes the cold-reader check, and check again after shortening.

proj, runtime = work / 'project', work / 'runtime'
blobs = json.loads((runtime / 'blobs.json').read_text()) if (runtime / 'blobs.json').exists() else {}

class H(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def translate_path(self, path):
        p = path.split('?')[0]
        if p.endswith('/support.js'): return str(runtime / 'dc-runtime.js')
        if p.startswith('/_blob/'):
            b = blobs.get(p[7:])
            if b: return str(runtime / b)
        return super().translate_path(path)
    def do_GET(self):
